name: Positivism
summary: Positivism, in its political form, is Auguste Comte's programme of rebuilding society on scientific knowledge after the French Revolution. It holds that thought passes from theological to metaphysical to scientific stages, that sociologists and a new moral priesthood should guide society as a spiritual power, and that order and progress go together. It replaces individual rights with duties, rejects popular sovereignty and class conflict, and in its later form proposes a non-supernatural Religion of Humanity built on altruism.
scope: Comtean positivism as a social and political doctrine: Comte's Course of Positive Philosophy and especially his System of Positive Polity (and its summary, A General View of Positivism), plus its later movements such as Brazilian and proletarian positivism. Answers follow Comte's mature doctrine. Logical positivism (the Vienna Circle), which is a philosophy of science with no political programme, and general scientific or empirical method are excluded. Many answers are low-confidence inferences, since Comte did not address modern issues.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Not addressed by Comte; inferred from his view that government is limited and provisional while the priesthood links hygiene and medicine to moral authority.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Not addressed by Comte; inferred from his preference for moral rather than legal regulation of wages by an industrial patriciate.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Comte rejected laissez-faire economics as a metaphysical doctrine and held that capitalists' activity must be guided by the spiritual power.

public-ownership.rationale: He held property to be social in nature but regulated by moral means, and kept private industrial leadership in place.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Not addressed by Comte; inferred from his moral rather than fiscal approach to the duties of the wealthy.

unions-good.rationale: Not addressed by Comte; inferred from his view that workers should be moral auxiliaries of the new spiritual power, not seek political power.

property-fundamental.rationale: Comte called property social in its nature and a public trust needing control, so it is not an absolute individual right.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Property and industry should be regulated, chiefly by moral pressure from the spiritual power rather than by law.

cut-welfare.rationale: Not addressed by Comte; inferred from the duty of the propertied to support workers' subsistence, which he treats as a moral obligation.

worker-ownership.rationale: He rejected communism's political solution and held that industry needs captains as well as workers.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Not addressed by Comte; inferred from his stress on order balanced against free speech.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Not addressed by Comte; inferred from his moral regulation of private life and his interest in hygiene.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: He favoured keeping freedom of speech even under the transitional dictatorship; inferred rather than stated about hate speech.

strong-leader.rationale: Comte favoured a temporary popular dictatorship during the transition and praised Napoleon III's 1851 coup.

state-harmful.rationale: Comte held that order requires centralised government and that government is needed to counter fragmentation.

limit-guns.rationale: Not addressed by Comte; inferred from order-oriented principles, with no recorded position.

empower-police-military.rationale: Comte thought the age of war was ending and wanted order through moral authority; inferred, with no stated position.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Not addressed by Comte; inferred from his insistence on moral regulation and indissoluble monogamy.

decide-locally.rationale: He favoured centralised order but also regional administrative divisions; no clear position on this question.

rehabilitation.rationale: Not addressed by Comte; inferred from his emphasis on moral education and the reform of feeling over force.

traditional-family.rationale: Comte made the family the basic unit of society, upheld indissoluble monogamy and placed women's main sphere in the home.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Not addressed by Comte; inferred from his support for monogamous marriage as the moral basis of the family.

abortion-legal.rationale: Not addressed by Comte; inferred from his family-centred, duty-based morality.

more-religion-public.rationale: He wanted public worship, rites and a calendar for a non-supernatural Religion of Humanity, though he rejected theology; the statement fits only loosely.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Not addressed by Comte; inferred from his humanitarian universalism, with no stated programme.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Comte tied women's affective role to biology and rejected modern claims of women's rights.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: He wanted a Western rather than purely national outlook but valued continuity of tradition; no clear position.

gradual-change.rationale: Order and progress, with reconstruction balanced against destruction, make social change orderly and cumulative.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Not addressed by Comte; inferred from his Western-republic internationalism, with no stated position.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: He envisaged a Western republic and an association of philosophers that is 'Occidental, not simply National'.

free-trade.rationale: Not addressed by Comte; inferred from his general scepticism of laissez-faire economics balanced by his internationalism.

nation-first.rationale: The philosophers' association was to be 'Occidental, not simply National', and he sought to weaken national prejudice.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Not addressed by Comte; inferred from a pacifist, humanity-centred outlook with no stated view.

open-borders.rationale: Not addressed by Comte; inferred from his Western-republic universalism, with no stated position.

limit-growth.rationale: Not addressed by Comte; inferred from his positive view of industry, with no position on environmental limits.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Not addressed by Comte; inferred from his trust in science and in guidance of action by prevision.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: His slogan was that science brings prevision and prevision brings action, though he held moral problems need moral solutions.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Not addressed by Comte; inferred from his faith in applied science.

revolution-justified.rationale: He saw revolution as a transitional phase that leads to anarchy unless reconstruction follows, and wanted to end the revolutionary period.

experts-over-public.rationale: Comte rejected popular sovereignty and gave guiding authority to scientists and sociologists as a spiritual power.

central-planning.rationale: He kept private industrial leaders, though under moral guidance, and did not propose a planned economy.

socialized-markets.rationale: Not addressed by Comte; inferred from his rejection of communism and his reliance on industrial captains.

land-value-tax.rationale: Not addressed by Comte; inferred from his general moral treatment of property, with no fiscal doctrine.

tax-inheritance.rationale: He treated inheritance as supporting the proper use of property.

basic-income.rationale: Not addressed by Comte; inferred from his view that workers' subsistence is a duty of the propertied and not an unconditional state entitlement.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Not addressed by Comte; inferred from no stated trade doctrine.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Not addressed by Comte; inferred from his view that capitalists perform the economy's function under moral guidance, not state direction.

widespread-small-property.rationale: He accepted concentrated capital under industrial 'captains' whose use of wealth is morally regulated.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: He rejected communism and expected workers to accept their position as public functionaries.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Not addressed by Comte; inferred from his centralist outlook, in which bankers form part of the industrial patriciate.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Not addressed by Comte; inferred from his organic view of social functions, though he placed no state bodies over wages.

one-party-rule.rationale: He called for a doctrine-led reorganisation, but spiritual power only counsels, so no state party is prescribed.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: He called for a republic of social sympathy but also courted Napoleon III and the Czar; he did not defend hereditary rule.

democracy-best.rationale: He opposed popular sovereignty and held that treating every citizen as competent on all social questions was an error.

direct-votes.rationale: He saw the claim that each citizen can decide every social question as a metaphysical error.

workers-councils.rationale: Workers' role is moral, as auxiliaries of the spiritual power, not political.

right-to-secede.rationale: Not addressed by Comte; inferred from no stated position; he wanted both centralisation and smaller republics.

natural-rulers.rationale: He held that a trained priesthood of scientists and sociologists is suited to guide society.

political-violence-never.rationale: He thought the age of war and violent revolution was ending and that spiritual power only counsels; he still allowed force against the gravest crimes.

war-builds-character.rationale: Comte believed the era of war was over and the industrial age was peaceful.

separate-church-state.rationale: Separating spiritual from temporal power is central to his polity.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: He called theology obsolete and workers should abandon it.

military-superiority.rationale: He expected an end to war and opposed European domination of the globe.

ethnic-nation.rationale: He pictured a Western association above national prejudice and based membership of Humanity on sociology.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Positivism is the 'party of construction' that reconciles order and progress, and workers and capitalists have complementary functions.

equal-outcomes.rationale: He held that industry needs captains and workers in differing functions, and workers should not seek wealth or power.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Not addressed by Comte; inferred from his opposition to European domination, with no position on land authority.

colonial-reparations.rationale: He opposed colonial domination, but reparations are an anachronistic question.

civilizational-union.rationale: He proposed a Western republic of nations bound by a shared positive religion.

self-interest-moral.rationale: His ethics centre on altruism ('live for others') and subordinating self-love to social love.

duties-before-rights.rationale: The epigraph of his General View says man's only right is to do his duty.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: His object of reverence is Humanity, not nature; inferred.

limit-population.rationale: Not addressed by Comte; inferred from no stated position.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: He saw industrial society as the positive stage and a basis for peace and progress.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Order is the basis of progress, and he feared dissolving change; inferred.

human-enhancement.rationale: Not addressed by Comte; inferred from no stated position.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Not addressed by Comte; inferred from his preference for expert guidance, balanced by his stress on moral feeling over calculation.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Not addressed by Comte; inferred from no stated position.

restore-past-order.rationale: He aimed at a new positive order, borrowing but rejecting Maistre's royalism and Catholicism.

results-over-ideology.rationale: He prized scientific method but built a comprehensive doctrine and polity; adherents would be split.

direct-action.rationale: He wanted moral reorganisation by opinion and a spiritual power, not street action or elections.

means-match-ends.rationale: Not addressed by Comte; inferred from no stated position.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Comte's law of three stages treats the scientific-industrial age as humanity's goal; he does not discuss foraging societies.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: He saw specialisation as fragmenting but wanted government and priesthood to coordinate it, not abolish it.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Not addressed by Comte; inferred from his rejection of communism, though he ties the rich to duties toward workers.

production-for-use.rationale: Not addressed by Comte; inferred from his view that industry serves society but that capital belongs to private captains.

profit-exploitation.rationale: He rejected the communist critique and held that capitalists perform society's nutritive function.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: He supported a temporary popular dictatorship but not class rule or class dominance.

collective-farming.rationale: Not addressed by Comte; inferred from his rejection of communism.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: He held that industrial society was ending the age of war.

taxation-theft.rationale: Not addressed by Comte; inferred from his view that property is social and a public trust.

harm-principle.rationale: He rejected liberal freedom of conscience and held that moral duty, not only harm, justifies social regulation.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Comte denied rights altogether, holding that people have only duties; that rejects group rights as much as individual ones, so the statement does not fit.

conscription.rationale: Not addressed by Comte; inferred from no stated position.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Not addressed by Comte; inferred from his centralism and rejection of individualism.

state-as-business.rationale: Not addressed by Comte; inferred from his view of government as moral and centralising.

positive-liberty.rationale: He held that society owes workers their material subsistence; inferred from this.

media-academia-power.rationale: Not addressed by Comte; inferred from his own proposal of a spiritual power, with no stated claim about media.

hereditarian-race.rationale: He grounded membership of Humanity in sociology, not biology; inferred.

organic-representation.rationale: He made the family the basic social unit, and his order rests on functions, not parties; the fit is loose.

total-state.rationale: He separated spiritual from temporal power and wanted counsel, not command, from the spiritual power.

national-rebirth.rationale: Not addressed by Comte; inferred from no stated position, though he wanted a moral reorganisation of society.

territorial-expansion.rationale: He opposed European domination and thought the age of war was over.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: His polity rests on spiritual guidance, not feudal oaths.

bound-labor.rationale: He wanted workers to be public functionaries, but nothing in his doctrine supports serfdom; inferred.

universal-morality.rationale: He grounded morality in Humanity and altruism, universal and scientifically studied, while subordinating intellect to feeling.

single-common-good.rationale: He held that the true principle of republicanism is all forces working together for the common good.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Not addressed by Comte; inferred from no stated position.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Not addressed by Comte; inferred from no stated position.

revive-national-language.rationale: Not addressed by Comte; inferred from no stated position.

workplace-democracy.rationale: He rejected popular sovereignty and kept industrial command with capitalists as captains.

school-vouchers.rationale: He wanted liberty of teaching free of government grants and control, and Positivist public instruction; vouchers are inferred.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Not addressed by Comte; inferred from no stated position.

economic-freedom.rationale: He rejected the liberal view of freedom as a metaphysical doctrine; inferred.

rule-by-example.rationale: True spiritual power gives counsel and never commands, and moral authority shapes opinion.

force-without-un.rationale: Not addressed by Comte; inferred from his hope for peace and a Western republic.

reason-over-faith.rationale: He held that the intellect should serve the heart and that affection is central, while rejecting supernatural faith.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Not addressed by Comte; inferred from no stated position.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Workers are public functionaries with a duty to work; inferred.

class-collaboration.rationale: Industry needs captains and workers in cooperation, and positivism seeks to reconcile classes under moral guidance.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: He honoured past figures in a positivist calendar and commemoration of the dead.

private-courts-defense.rationale: He held that order requires centralised government and that force remains for the gravest crimes, so defence is not for private firms.

national-self-determination.rationale: Not addressed by Comte; inferred from his Western-republic outlook above national prejudice.

dominated-front.rationale: Not addressed by Comte; inferred from his Western-republic outlook.

workers-nation.rationale: He saw the proletariat as natural allies in a Western, not national, movement.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Comte placed women's main sphere in the family and gave them a moral rather than political role, rejecting modern claims of equal public power.

ban-interest.rationale: Not addressed by Comte; inferred from his keeping private industrial and financial leadership in place, regulated by moral pressure rather than legal prohibition.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Not addressed directly; inferred from the Religion of Humanity, which rests on altruism and the unity of the whole human race.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Comte rejected class conflict and held that order rests on moral guidance from the spiritual power, so government is not mainly a tool of one class.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Not addressed by Comte; inferred from his support for industrial development guided by a spiritual power, with no stance on energy sources.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Comte looked toward a single Western republic and shared humanity rather than national cultures; inferred, with no stated view on immigration.

elite-replacement.rationale: Inferred from Comte's rationalist, science-based outlook, which has no place for conspiracy explanations of social change.

proportional-representation.rationale: Comte rejected popular sovereignty and counting votes, so electoral formulas are secondary; inferred disfavour of party-vote politics.

national-mission.rationale: Comte opposed conquest and held that peoples should not impose themselves; inferred, though the West was to lead others morally.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Comte held women to be morally superior but assigned them a domestic role and rejected equality of function, so he denied a systematic disadvantage needing correction.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Comte criticised parliamentary politicians and metaphysical lawyers yet wanted a governing patriciate; inferred as split.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Comte predates eugenics and grounded social order in duty and education; inferred opposition to coercive state steering of births.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Inferred from Comte's emphasis on duties and on moral judgement of public conduct by the spiritual power.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Comte rejected laissez-faire economics and gave government and the spiritual power wider moral and social roles than defence, courts and property.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Comte did not address race mixing; inferred from his ideal of a single fraternal Humanity, though he shared some period racial assumptions.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Comte replaces individual rights with duties and holds that functions and capacities form a natural hierarchy, so equal legal rights as such are not his principle.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Comte rejects revolutionary agitation and looks to gradual moral reorganisation under a spiritual power; inferred, since he never debated socialism in one country.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Comte opposed colonial conquest as a stage of the military past and wanted dependencies to go free; inferred for settler displacement.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Inferred from a single universal Religion of Humanity and a spiritual power separate from state law, which leave no place for community-specific civil codes.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Comte demanded freedom of teaching and separation of spiritual and temporal powers, so legal policing of conversion is unlikely; inferred.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Comte urged kindness to animals as a moral duty but through moral influence, not coercive law; inferred.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Positive education was meant to replace theology; inferred that doctrinal religious teaching would be withdrawn from public schooling.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Comte saw government as limited and provisional, and Marxist state theory is not his; no basis to say either way.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Comte explicitly rejects popular sovereignty and the doctrine of rights; legitimacy rests on competence and moral authority, not consent.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Comte held that positive science yields objective knowledge that the spiritual power uses to guide society, though his maxim that everything is relative complicates the picture.

trade-surplus.rationale: Comte looked to a cosmopolitan Western Republic and industrial peace rather than national economic rivalry; mercantilist surplus-seeking is inferred as foreign to him.

population-transfer.rationale: Comte opposed forced conquest and favoured moral persuasion by the spiritual power; expulsion of minorities is inferred as contrary to this.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Comte replaced individual rights with duties and accepted authoritative social direction, so an absolute non-aggression principle is not his; inferred.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Comte stressed altruism, social solidarity and cooperation, and sought to replace conflict with order and progress.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Comte favoured strong order and a unified social doctrine and had no commitment to unlimited party pluralism; inferred.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Comte rejected liberty as an individual right and favoured duty and moral guidance; non-domination as a concept is inferred as peripheral to him.

separated-powers.rationale: Comte's central institutional idea separates spiritual power (the priesthood) from temporal power (government and industry) so each checks the other.

vanguard-party.rationale: Comte rejected class conflict and revolution and gave guidance to a spiritual priesthood of sociologists rather than a revolutionary party; inferred.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Comte held that property is a social function with duties, and that the proletariat deserves moral and social attention from the priesthood and the rich.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Comte did not address council housing; inferred from his view that property is a social trust held with duties, which cuts both ways.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Comte rejected class conflict and urged workers to seek moral influence and not coercion; inferred he would limit strikes, though he never addressed the question.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Comte tied social ills to moral and intellectual disorder and not to numbers; inferred, as he gave no population theory of poverty.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Comte sought a unified Western republic bound by a shared religion of humanity and sympathy; inferred he would not see diversity as the cause of conflict.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Comte rejected popular sovereignty and wanted rule guided by scientific and moral experts, and chance selection of rulers contradicts that; inferred.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Comte accepted a temporary republican dictatorship to restore order in a crisis; inferred for emergency powers, as he never discussed modern legal protections.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Comte did not address price controls; inferred from his view that wealth is held as a social trust, set against his wish for limited government.

party-controls-media.rationale: Comte wanted opinion guided by a spiritual priesthood separate from government, so state control of the media is not his model; inferred.

party-commands-army.rationale: Comte wanted spiritual power separate from temporal power and rejected party rule; inferred, as he did not discuss command of the army.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Comte did not address naturalization; nothing in his doctrine settles the length of residence required.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Not addressed directly; inferred from Comte's view of office as a social function and duty rather than a means to wealth.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Inferred from Comte's subordination of the individual to the social whole and duties over rights.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Inferred from Comte's vision of a Western republic of federated small states united under common moral guidance.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Comte favoured a republican dictatorship with concentrated executive power and a weak assembly.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Inferred from the positivist priesthood's own hierarchy with authority from above.

clerical-rule.rationale: Comte separated spiritual from temporal power, so the priesthood advises morally and does not rule.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Comte opposed war and favoured Western unity, but did not preach defeat of one's own government; inferred.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Inferred from Comte's subordination of art to morality, with the spiritual power guiding it by public opinion.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Inferred from Comte's rejection of elections and popular sovereignty; no term limits for capable rulers.

recall-officials.rationale: Comte rejected popular sovereignty and the idea that voters command officials.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Comte favoured peace and a Western union, but alliances as such are not addressed.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Comte kept private property but with social duties; the question is not directly addressed, so this is inferred.

people-in-arms.rationale: Comte expected the military spirit to give way to industry, but did not address citizen militias; inferred.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Inferred: Comte centred his reorganised society on cities and an urban priesthood.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Inferred from Comte proposal to split large states into small republics.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Comte held that scientifically educated sociologists should guide society as the spiritual power.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: The law of three stages ranks societies by how far they have advanced.

death-penalty.rationale: Inferred from Comte altruism and humane ethic; he did not set out a position on capital punishment.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Comte prescribed priestly encyclopedic education and a domestic role for women; adherents are split.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Positivism holds the theological stage is superseded by scientific knowledge.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Inferred from the moral authority Comte gave to the priesthood and public opinion over private conduct.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Comte rejected revealed religion and replaced individual rights with duties; inferred.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Inferred from Comte replacing individual rights with social duties and subordination.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Comte stressed social order and the duties attached to wealth, not cancellation of obligations; inferred.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Comte sought moral and intellectual reorganization by a spiritual power rather than overthrow of the property order; inferred.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Comte rejected popular sovereignty and the revolutionary politics of assemblies in favour of expert guidance.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Comte accepted temporary dictatorship and rejected freedom of conscience as a dogma in favour of order.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Comte made altruism and service to Humanity central, so duties to the poor of any land are inferred.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Nuclear weapons are anachronistic; Comte wanted peace and small republics but also a strong state. Neither answer is clearly implied.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Comte rejected popular sovereignty and universal suffrage as the source of authority.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Comte did not address central banking; he trusted bankers as industrial leaders under moral supervision.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Comte wanted large states broken into small republics and valued peace, but nothing settles territorial claims. Not addressed.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Comte held that property is a social function whose holders owe duties to society, guided by the priesthood.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Comte lived before the USSR and positivists generally reject class conflict; the label is not addressed. Inferred.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Comte's scientific foresight ('know in order to foresee') favours expert guidance, but he never addressed acting before certainty; inferred.

collective-defense.rationale: Comte hoped for peace among Western republics and opposed conquest, but gave no view on mutual-defence pacts; inferred.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Comte condemned conquest and wanted large states broken into small republics, so annexation without consent would not be legitimate; inferred.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Comte separated spiritual from temporal power so that neither dominates the other, which rules out placing the clergy under civil authority.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Comte wanted a republican dictatorship checked by priestly moral authority and rejected party politics, but did not describe a unifying symbolic head; inferred.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Comte favoured dividing large states into small republics, so holding a region by force runs against his programme; inferred.

region-keeps-system.rationale: His preference for small, self-governing republics suggests regions could keep their own arrangements; inferred.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Positivism replaces the theological stage with a scientific one and rejects divine right.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Not addressed by Comte, who left wealth to be regulated morally by the industrial patriciate; inferred.

character-from-environment.rationale: Comte held that education and social influence shape people but also assumed innate affective tendencies; inferred as split.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Comte's temporal ruler is bound by the duties and moral counsel of the spiritual power, though his dictatorship is strong; inferred.

space-expansion.rationale: Positivism centres its cult on Humanity and the Earth, so expansion into space is not a goal; inferred.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Comte rejected parliamentary balance of powers and popular sovereignty in favour of concentrated executive power; inferred.

leader-cult.rationale: The cult is directed to Humanity, not to a national leader, though Comte accepted a strong dictatorial executive; inferred.

equal-parenting.rationale: Comte did not address custody; his stress on family roles gives no clear direction; inferred.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: Comte rejected class conflict and held that order and progress go together through moral and spiritual guidance.

land-redistribution.rationale: Comte kept private property, held under social duty and moral control; seizing estates is inferred to be rejected.

refugee-return.rationale: Not addressed by Comte; no basis for a position.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Comte favored small republics and limits on state extension beyond natural territories, so claiming territory by nationality is rejected.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Comte's spiritual power works by persuasion, not state punishment; inferred.

women-must-cover.rationale: Comte placed women in the family with moral influence, not legal compulsion; inferred.

common-currency.rationale: Comte envisioned a Western unity of republics under a shared spiritual outlook; inferred for a currency union.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Comte proposed a fraternal union of Western peoples above national separatism; inferred.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Comte did not address national minorities.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Comte's law of three stages makes intellectual development the prime mover of society, not economic conditions.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Comte rejected popular sovereignty, so courts limiting majorities fit; inferred.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Comte placed women's main sphere in the family and rejected modern claims of women's rights.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Comte was anti-colonial and favored cooperation among Western nations; inferred.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Comte stressed workers' moral and social protection; inferred.

moral-incentives.rationale: Comte's altruism and duties over rights call for living for others, supporting moral over material motives.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Positivism holds that reconstruction, not destruction, is needed, with order accompanying progress.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Comte opposed hereditary aristocracy but kept hereditary transmission of property; no clear position.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Comte taught history as the story of Humanity as a whole, with a calendar honoring figures across civilizations, rather than of one nation.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Comte condemned conquest and colonial rule by force while holding that the West should guide others by persuasion; inferred.

patriotic-education.rationale: Comte put attachment to Humanity above the nation, though he saw the fatherland as a stage of altruism; inferred.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from his view that social roles should reflect function and capacity, not birth or group claims.

public-money-creation.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from Comte's plan to have banking centralized and directed by a patriciate for social ends rather than private gain.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Comte rejected revolution and class war and sought social harmony under moral guidance; inferred that capitalism can be reformed and stabilized.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Not addressed; Comte opposed conquest and favored a federation of republics, so he would reject imperial claims; inferred.

delink-world-market.rationale: Not addressed; Comte envisioned the unity of Humanity and Western leadership, so delinking runs against it; inferred.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: Comte rejected class conflict and saw workers and employers as bound by mutual duty; inferred as hostile to a labor-aristocracy thesis.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Comte replaced individual rights with duties and treated property as a social function, so owners have no right to refuse on any ground.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Comte rejected natural rights as a metaphysical doctrine and replaced them with duties, so a rights document would be opposed.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Comte did not address colonial treaties; adherents offer no clear position.

elective-rulers.rationale: Comte rejected popular sovereignty and proposed rule by a dictatorial executive guided by the spiritual power; inferred against election as legitimacy.

minority-veto.rationale: Comte rejected individual rights in favour of duties and social order, so a one-member veto is inferred to be rejected.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Comte emphasised order and the duty of obedience, and rejected a right of insurrection; inferred.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Comte rejected popular sovereignty and parliamentary government in favour of a strong executive guided by expert opinion; inferred.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: The Religion of Humanity extends altruistic duty to other living beings; inferred, not firmly sourced.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Inferred from altruism toward animals combined with an acceptance of their use by industrial society.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Positivism replaces rights with duties and calls the wealthy to use property as a social trust, in line with its altruist ethic.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Positivism holds that individuals live for others and society through duties, so withdrawal is rejected, though Comte kept rulers separate from the spiritual power.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Comte wanted the spiritual power to shape opinion for social harmony and treated this as positive, not as manipulation; inferred.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Comte held that public opinion shaped by the spiritual power, not force, should sustain order; inferred.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Comte rejected class conflict theories; dependency theory is anachronistic and inferred to be rejected.

native-born-offices.rationale: The Religion of Humanity is universalist; inferred.

party-own-road.rationale: Anachronistic; the statement concerns communist parties, not Comte's programme.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Comte did not address foreign aid; inferred as neutral.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Comte proposed dissolving large states into small republics and favoured peace over conquest; inferred.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Inferred from universalism and rejection of hereditary claims to authority.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Anachronistic; Comte lived before fascism and no positivist position is documented.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Anachronistic; adherents are not documented as taking a side.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: Comte opposed slavery as incompatible with humanity; inferred that slavery would be named as the cause.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Positivism venerates the past through the cult of Humanity and a calendar of great figures; inferred.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Anachronistic; Comte set separate roles for the sexes and no position on modern programmes.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Comte treated women as morally superior, to be protected; inferred he would not equate the two.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Positivism claims a single universal law of social evolution, so institutions are expected to converge; inferred.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Comte viewed industrial society as superseding the military stage; inferred.

paid-care-work.rationale: Comte kept women in the domestic sphere supported by men, and no payment for domestic work is documented; inferred.

filial-duty.rationale: Comte made reverence for ancestors and the family the school of altruism, with duties of children to parents central to the positive family.

office-by-exam.rationale: Not addressed directly; inferred from Comte's rule by trained competence under a spiritual power and his rejection of popular election.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Not addressed by Comte; inferred only from his view that wealth is a social trust, which points neither clearly for nor against such blocks.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Comte held marriage to be indissoluble, urging perpetual widowhood, so divorce on demand runs against his polity.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Comte rejected popular sovereignty and mandated representatives, placing guidance in a priesthood and a provisional executive.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Inferred from Comte's view that capital is held as a social trust under moral control, which sits badly with purely private retirement saving.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Inferred from Comte's defence of property as a social function: private holding is kept, but under moral duty to use it for society.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Inferred from Comte's hostility to parliamentary rule and debate; he favoured a strong executive checked by moral opinion, not legislative control.

single-official-language.rationale: Comte's Western Republic envisaged smaller states with local tongues beside shared education; he gave no clear line on imposing one language.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Inferred from Comte's cosmopolitan Religion of Humanity and dislike of national exclusion; he gave no direct view on land ownership.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Inferred from Comte's stress on duties and order and his rejection of rights-based claims; he did not address discrimination law.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Inferred from Comte's altruism and subordination of personal appetite to social duty, with wealth treated as a trust rather than an end.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Comte saw industrial society as ending conquest and war, so backing armed rebellion in other countries conflicts with his doctrine.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Inferred from Comte's condemnation of conquest and forced rule over other peoples; he wanted peaceful moral union of the West.

corporate-influence.rationale: Comte expected the spiritual power to moralise wealth-holders and make property a social function, so he would criticise plutocratic influence; inferred.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Comte looked to a Western fraternity beyond nations and disliked nationalism; inferred opposition to sovereignty-based funding limits.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Comte stressed the family but did not address population policy; inferred neutral.

residents-only-property.rationale: Comte treated property as a social function but did not address local residency restrictions; inferred neutral.

job-guarantee.rationale: Comte held that society owes the proletariat stable subsistence and employment as a duty; inferred support for guaranteed work.

democratic-peace.rationale: Comte argued industrial society makes war obsolete and looked to a pacific Western republic; inferred mild agreement.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Comte replaced individual rights with duties and held that everyone owes service to Humanity, so a claim of no general duty to obey would be rejected.

non-intervention.rationale: Comte favoured peaceful moral influence and small republics but did not address intervention; inferred neutral.

industrial-unions.rationale: Comte backed industrial workers' moral organisation but did not specify union structure; inferred neutral.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Positivist emphasis on science and solidarity rejects scapegoating of minorities; inferred.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Comte exalted marriage as a lasting moral institution under social regulation, so he would reject abolishing its legal standing.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Comte prized public opinion as a moral force but entrusted guidance to an expert spiritual power; inferred split.

local-production.rationale: Comte did not address local production; inferred neutral.

informal-organisation.rationale: Comte organised the Positivist Church as a formal hierarchy, so he disfavoured purely informal groups; inferred.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Comte's Western republic and duty to Humanity subordinate national sovereignty to wider morality; inferred.

religious-nation.rationale: The Religion of Humanity is non-supernatural and universal rather than national, so a nation defined by one religion is disfavoured; inferred.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from Comte's vision of a peaceful Western Republic of equals under a shared spiritual power, not tributary hierarchy.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Inferred from Comte's emphasis on social solidarity and unity, which cuts against regions keeping their revenue.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Comte kept private property but held that it is a social function under moral control, and did not propose common ownership of the means of production.

defeat-communism.rationale: Comte opposed communism as destructive of family and property but sought to win it over by moral persuasion rather than defeat it; inferred.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Not addressed by Comte, who wanted a limited government and moral rather than legal regulation; inferred and split.

religion-illusion.rationale: Mixed: Comte saw theological belief as a stage that will be outgrown, yet held that religion meets lasting needs and founded the Religion of Humanity to meet them.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Inferred from Comte's view of the industrial stage as a necessary phase of progress, though he criticized its moral failings.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Comte placed women's sphere in the family and did not tie their status to the economic system; inferred.

socialized-care.rationale: Comte made the family the basic social unit and women's moral role in it central, so domestic care stays private.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from Comte's cosmopolitan Western unity and preference for moral persuasion over compulsion.

treaties-binding.rationale: Comte rejected individual rights and popular sovereignty and did not address such treaties; inferred and split.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Comte wanted small republics within a Western union but not common property; communal self-governing property is not his programme.

majority-settlement.rationale: Inferred from Comte's opposition to conquest and his support for peaceful, voluntary union.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Comte presented positivism as a way past both retrograde and revolutionary doctrines; inferred as a third course.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Inferred from Comte's Religion of Humanity, which put humanity above nations and rejected theological claims such as sacred land.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Positivism rests on established scientific and historical knowledge, so denying documented facts conflicts with its method.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Inferred from Comte's view that moral norms are enforced by the spiritual power's persuasion rather than law; his own sexual morality was strict.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Comte favored a strong temporary government to restore order, but vested spiritual authority in a priesthood of persuasion; inferred.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Comte held the spiritual power should rule by persuasion, not force, and treated theology as outdated, so punishing blasphemy is rejected.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Inferred from Comte's view of industrial society as peaceful and his opposition to conquest.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: Inferred from Comte's view that theology is a superseded stage and that Humanity, not a god, is the object of duty.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Comte held that the theological stage is superseded, so religious law is not a basis of legitimacy.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Comte rejected popular sovereignty and metaphysical rights, leaving decisions to the competent under the spiritual power's guidance.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Comte rejected class conflict and proposed moral unity under a spiritual power, not an oppression-based analysis.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Inferred from Comte's fixed views of sex roles, which treated women's and men's functions as natural.

assisted-dying.rationale: Inferred from Comte's duty-based ethics and Religion of Humanity's emphasis on social ties; not addressed.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Comte's slogan of order and progress aimed to join the conservative and revolutionary strands, so he would agree.

alienated-labor.rationale: Inferred from Comte, who saw industrial work as a social function and held that moral education, not abolition of capitalism, solves its ills.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Inferred; Comte's calendar honored Muhammad and his Religion of Humanity treated religions as stages, not as civilizational enemies.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Comte held that theology is a superseded stage of thought and placed authority in science and the priesthood of humanity, not God.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Inferred from Comte's separation of spiritual from temporal power, which implies a state free of religious establishment.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Inferred from Comte's view that employers hold wealth as a social trust under moral regulation.

social-market-economy.rationale: Inferred from Comte's industrial patriciate and moral regulation of markets, a middle path between laissez-faire and state control.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Inferred from Comte's view that the military stage of society is giving way to the industrial one, though he kept temporal government.

rich-first.rationale: Inferred from Comte's industrial patriciate, which holds wealth as a social trust and moves society step by step.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Inferred; Comte pictured a Western republic of fraternal peoples rather than rival blocs, but did not address alliances.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Inferred: Comte replaced heredity with a ruler chosen by merit and nominated by his predecessor, so succession by a child is not his rule, though he did not oppose all inheritance.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Inferred: Comte placed finance in the hands of private bankers as a patriciate with moral duties, and did not propose user-owned credit.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Inferred: Comte did not address international lenders; his stress on order and industrial duty gives no clear answer.

property-franchise.rationale: Inferred: Comte rejected popular sovereignty and elections altogether, and he did not propose a property qualification for the vote.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Inferred: Comte praised women's moral influence while assigning them to the family, and he held that humanity should master nature through science, so he would not join the two causes.

reification.rationale: Inferred: Comte criticised economic individualism and wanted capital moral duties, but he also defended private property and industry, and the reification theory is Marxist.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Inferred: Comte distrusted unlimited freedom of the press and thought the wealthy bear moral duties as patricians, so the claim as framed is not his.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Inferred: Comte favoured government guided by positive science and moral authority, and it is unclear whether he endorsed a rule of publicly announced law.

racial-franchise.rationale: Comte's Religion of Humanity is universal, with the unity of all peoples as its aim, so a racial limit on rights contradicts it.

online-participation.rationale: Inferred: Comte rejected popular sovereignty and rule by public opinion on political questions, so open mass deliberation is not part of his programme.

open-government-data.rationale: Inferred: Comte gave public opinion a moral role in checking rulers, which favours publicity of public acts, though he did not write on open data.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Inferred: Comte wanted a shared spiritual faith but a universal one, and he did not recommend legal restrictions on marriage between religions.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: The Religion of Humanity rests on universal altruism and fellowship, so boycotting people for their religion contradicts it.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Comte rejected popular sovereignty and wanted society guided by scientific expertise and a spiritual power, not by ordinary citizens deciding public questions.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Inferred from Comte replacing theology with a rationally grounded Religion of Humanity, which treats inherited religion as something to be rebuilt for the scientific age.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Comte treats property as a social trust with duties attached and wants moral pressure on the wealthy; inferred, since he did not frame it as a liberty question.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from Comte's traditional view of family, sex and moral order.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Comte replaces theology with a Religion of Humanity taught by a spiritual power kept separate from the state, so the state does not run an atheist education.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Order is half of the positivist motto and Comte wants social discipline upheld by moral and governmental authority, not dissolved.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Not addressed by Comte; his unitary, authority-centred polity gives no clear answer about communal power-sharing.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Comte relies on altruism and moral duty of the patriciate rather than rights-based state claims; inferred.

term-limits.rationale: Comte favoured strong, continuous executive authority rather than rotation; inferred.

vote-delegation.rationale: Positivism rejects popular sovereignty and the individual political right to vote, favouring duties and guidance by experts and the priesthood.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Humanity as the object of worship implies concern for its continuity; Comte never discussed extinction risk, so inferred.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Comte exalted women as moral guides of the family but reserved the priesthood roles to men; inferred from his system.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Comte held that women's role is moral influence in the home, with the family hierarchy preserved and marriage indissoluble.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Comte stressed patriotic attachment to one's own country, though his Religion of Humanity is universal; not addressed on local voting. Inferred.

rent-control.rationale: Comte wanted moral rather than legal regulation of economic life; rent caps were not addressed. Inferred.

abolish-ip.rationale: Comte held property to be a social function held in trust, so IP is not an absolute right, but he did not call for abolishing it. Inferred.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Comte wanted the young educated by the spiritual power, not drilled for national service. Inferred.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Anachronistic; Comte did not address nuclear weapons. Inferred from his preference for peace between small republics.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Anachronistic; Comte did not address foreign bases. Inferred from his support for small autonomous republics.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Comte's Religion of Humanity stresses collective memory and altruism, which favours recording wrongs done to a people. Inferred.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Comte treated property as a social function and wealth as held for the benefit of society, so income should follow useful work.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Comte accepted defensive force but looked to a future of peace and the moral priesthood; not a pacifist. Inferred.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Comte's three stages treat origin myths as theological or metaphysical thinking, to be replaced by scientific history. Inferred.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Comte took sex differences as natural and biological, assigning women a distinct moral role. Inferred.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Comte saw women as a distinct moral class with a defined role. Inferred.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Comte's calendar of great men honours the dead who served humanity, but honours by service to humanity, not nation. Inferred.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Comte replaced theological and metaphysical thought with positive science and so did not frame politics as a spiritual war of good and evil. Inferred.

culture-before-state.rationale: For Comte the spiritual power and moral reform of beliefs and opinions must precede and guide political action.

god-not-male.rationale: Comte rejected theology, so statements about God do not apply; he did venerate Woman as a moral ideal. Inferred.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Comte held women to be morally superior yet limited their role to the home, so he would partly agree. Inferred.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Comte stressed the unity of humanity and rejected group economic preference. Inferred.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Comte favoured breaking up large states into small republics, but not by merging regions by people. Inferred.

independent-unions.rationale: Not addressed; Comte wanted workers to have moral influence but opposed class conflict and strikes, so this is inferred as split.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Inferred from Comte's rejection of class conflict and popular sovereignty: order is built by moral and scientific guides, not worker rule.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from Comte's view that capital is held as a social trust by industrial leaders.

second-chamber.rationale: Inferred from Comte's rejection of parliamentary government and of balancing powers in favor of a separate spiritual power.

municipal-property.rationale: Inferred from Comte's view that property is a social function held by industrial leaders, not by the commune.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Inferred from Comte's plan for small republics coordinated by a spiritual power rather than a sovereign state.

family-wage.rationale: Inferred from Comte's concern that workers have a secure living and a family life.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: Not addressed; Comte valued science yet also expert guidance and caution.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: Inferred from Comte's faith in science improving human life, and the Religion of Humanity's care for humanity.

anonymous-payments.rationale: Inferred from Comte's stress on social and moral authority over private conduct.

online-anonymity.rationale: Inferred from Comte's emphasis on public opinion and moral supervision over private conduct.

person-over-state.rationale: Comte replaces individual rights with duties and has individuals live for Humanity, so the person is subordinated to the social whole.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Comte's later Religion of Humanity answers a human need for feeling and worship in non-supernatural form.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Inferred from Comte's view that governments are provisional and subordinate to a spiritual power.

gm-crops.rationale: Inferred from Comte's trust in applied science to improve human life.

dense-cities.rationale: Not addressed; Comte's cities were small and moral, but he said nothing on density and environment.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Inferred from Comte's universal Humanity, which counts all humans as one family.

racial-pride.rationale: Inferred from Comte's universal Humanity, which discourages pride tied to race.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Inferred from Comte's view that industrial society makes military conquest obsolete.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Comte looked toward a universal Humanity and small republics rather than language-based nations; inferred.

communal-electorates.rationale: Comte rejected popular sovereignty and electoral politics in favour of moral guidance and duties; inferred.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Comte did not address such plots; his outlook is pacific and universalist, inferred.

free-public-college.rationale: Comte put education under the spiritual power and wanted it universal; free provision is inferred.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Comte did not address pollution or resource pricing.

future-generations.rationale: Comte's Humanity binds the living to the dead and to future generations, implying a duty to those yet to come.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Comte held that women's affective, moral qualities are central to social life and the Religion of Humanity.

arms-reduction.rationale: Comte thought modern industrial society should outgrow military conquest; inferred.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Comte did not address diplomatic secrecy.

capital-controls.rationale: Comte did not address capital movements and the sources give no basis for a view.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Inferred from Comte's emphasis on social order and a unified authority; he did not discuss it directly.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Comte condemned conquest as obsolete in the industrial age yet prized order and discipline; inferred split.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Comte wanted harmony between workers and employers through moral influence and the priesthood, not adversarial bargaining; inferred.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Comte held that wealth is a social trust guided by moral duty, not state income top-ups; tax credits are anachronistic and inferred.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Anachronistic; Comte favoured small provisional governments but gave no fiscal rule doctrine.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Comte looked to a moral federation of Western republics, not redistribution through economic rules; inferred.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Comte sought orderly reorganisation under spiritual authority and opposed revolutionary upheaval as a prolonged crisis.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: Comte planned a fixed scientific blueprint for society, so no open experimentation with systems.

nature-as-capital.rationale: Anachronistic; Comte valued the Earth as part of the Great Medium, but did not price it.

sacred-nation.rationale: Comte's object of devotion was Humanity, with small fatherlands as stepping stones; he opposed nationalist worship, inferred.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Anachronistic; Comte wanted free public education but not debt cancellation, inferred.

internal-colonialism.rationale: Not a positivist concept; inferred from Comte's organic-unity view of society.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Comte grounded sociology in a universal human nature and the Religion of Humanity, and held that it develops only within natural laws.

public-service-media.rationale: Anachronistic; Comte wanted the priesthood to control opinion and education and distrusted a free press, so this is split.

religions-one-truth.rationale: Comte held that all theological religions belong to a superseded stage and should be replaced by the Religion of Humanity, not that they share one truth; inferred from his stages theory.

farm-price-support.rationale: Not addressed; Comte's priesthood and industrial patriciate would guide the economy morally but he did not discuss price supports.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Anachronistic; Comte opposed war between advanced nations, but inferring a stance on nuclear arms is uncertain.

workers-own-party.rationale: Comte rejected class conflict and political parties in favour of the proletariat's moral union with the spiritual power; inferred from that.

ban-fgm.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the Religion of Humanity's altruism and Comte's wish to have a moral authority suppress harmful customs.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Comte placed women in the family sphere and rejected modern claims of women's rights, so equal inheritance is inferred as unlikely to be endorsed.

one-language-many-names.rationale: Comte proposed a common Western language eventually, but the question of naming regional varieties is not addressed.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: Inferred from Comte's rejection of individual rights and rule by expert, moral authority over litigation by individuals.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: Comte wanted advisory moral power in a priesthood of scientists, not hereditary or customary chiefs; inferred.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: Comte replaced individual rights with duties to society and humanity, so liberty gives way to collective ends; environmental concern is anachronistic and inferred.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Not addressed; Comte stressed order and moral education over punishment but the specific question was not discussed.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: Inferred from Comte's stress on social cohesion and shared moral and cultural bonds in a unified society.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Not addressed by Comte; he rejected class conflict and favoured workers' moral organisation, but said nothing on compulsion.

voter-id.rationale: Not addressed; Comte rejected popular sovereignty and elections as such, so the rules for voting are not his concern.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: Inferred from Comte's separation of the spiritual and temporal powers, with freedom of teaching and no state religion.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Comte rejected popular sovereignty and the idea that election legitimates rule; legitimacy comes from serving social order and progress.

premarital-sex.rationale: Comte stressed chastity, lifelong monogamous marriage and women's moral role; the sources do not discuss premarital sex directly.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: Anachronistic; Comte did not address it, and his priesthood and public opinion, not state coercion, were meant to keep order.

negative-income-tax.rationale: Inferred from Comte's replacement of rights with duties, and of public welfare with the moral duty of employers.

women-suffrage.rationale: Comte denied political rights as such and kept women to a moral, domestic role, so he opposed women's public office.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: Inferred from Comte's Religion of Humanity, which exalts women as moral guides, and his view of religion as social bond.

race-social-construct.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; Comte's stage theory and the doctrine's later movements pull in different directions.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: Inferred from Comte's rejection of equality of the sexes in function and of rights-based state programmes.

homestead-ownership.rationale: Inferred from Comte's view that property is a social function held in trust, not a natural right.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: Inferred from Comte's vision of a moral Western Republic and the rule of positive morality over nations.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: Comte held that theological thought is a superseded stage, so literal scripture is rejected.

gendered-self-government.rationale: Inferred from Comte's duty-based view assigning women a moral role in the family rather than public office.

defend-planned-state.rationale: Inferred from Comte's rejection of class conflict and of revolutionary socialism.

indirect-election.rationale: Inferred from Comte's rejection of popular sovereignty in favor of guidance by capable leaders.

national-church-status.rationale: Comte replaced established religion with the Religion of Humanity, so no church holds special status.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: Inferred from Comte's plan to divide large states into small republics.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: Inferred from Comte's rejection of popular sovereignty and of deciding questions by majority vote.

simple-living.rationale: Inferred from Comte's emphasis on altruism and duty and the moderate wants of his positive society.

equal-conscription.rationale: Inferred from Comte's separation of women's moral role from public and military life.

homeland-spiritual-bond.rationale: Inferred from Comte's Religion of Humanity, which gives devotion to Humanity rather than to a national land.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: Inferred from Comte's stress on moral duty and a spiritual power restraining rulers, which rules out arbitrary killing by the state.

close-ties-china.rationale: Not addressed by Comte; foreign alignment between modern powers is inferred as irrelevant to his doctrine.

protect-kin-minorities.rationale: Inferred from Comte's plan to split large states into small republics and his priority of Humanity over nations.

resources-common-ownership.rationale: Comte held that property is a social function with duties; the modern idea of compensation for resources is inferred as outside his thought.

self-ownership.rationale: Comte replaces individual rights with duties and holds that no one has a right over themselves apart from social service.

cut-consumption-tax.rationale: Not addressed by Comte; his provisional, limited government gives no position on specific taxes.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: Not addressed by Comte; inferred as split between his moral-help approach and his collective view of social duty.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: Comte favoured a strong executive and rejected parliamentary sovereignty, but gave the priesthood and patriciate a mediating role, so inferred as split.

no-business-privileges.rationale: Inferred from Comte's industrial patriciate subject to moral duty, which does not favour privilege for the well-connected.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: Comte separated spiritual from temporal power and put a single Religion of Humanity above sects, so denominational politics is inferred as foreign to it.

tech-with-ancestral-values.rationale: Inferred from Comte's aim to combine science and industry with veneration of the past and of the dead.

wife-divorce-without-consent.rationale: Inferred from Comte's view of women as morally superior but kept within the family role, and his disfavour of divorce.

national-resource-control.rationale: Not addressed by Comte; inferred as outside his doctrine.

distribution-by-process.rationale: Comte treats property as a social function carrying duties, so fairness is not settled by acquisition alone.

financial-transactions-tax.rationale: Not addressed by Comte; inferred as neither supported nor opposed given his moral rather than legal regulation of finance.

racism-not-main-obstacle.rationale: Not addressed by Comte; inferred from his emphasis on moral reform that the sources do not apply to racial disadvantage.

unjust-law-not-binding.rationale: Not addressed directly; Comte replaces rights with duties and puts moral authority in the spiritual power, but also stresses order, so inferred as split.

automate-paid-work.rationale: Not addressed by Comte; inferred as split between his industrial progress and his stress on the dignity of the worker's role.

multipolar-world.rationale: Inferred from Comte's vision of a unified Western republic and humanity under shared guidance, not rival independent centres.

labour-theory-of-value.rationale: Not a Comtean doctrine; he saw wealth as a social product of collective effort, so he is inferred to reject labour alone as its source.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: Comte ranked love of Humanity above country while valuing local attachments and the proletariat; inferred as split.

material-over-identity.rationale: Comte put moral and social reform ahead of material class demands and also supported the workers, so inferred as split.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: Inferred from Comte's rejection of class conflict and of popular sovereignty in favour of a moral priesthood, not party rule over a market.

missingStatements.text: Society needs a shared secular faith, centred on humanity rather than God, to hold it together.
missingStatements.rationale: Comte's Religion of Humanity was meant to give positivist societies the cohesion traditional worship gave.

missingStatements.text: Women's proper sphere is the family rather than public power.
missingStatements.rationale: Comte placed women's main sphere in the family and rejected modern claims of women's rights.

notes: Mill separated the 'good Comte' of the Course from the 'bad Comte' of the Polity; this profile follows the Polity, which holds the political doctrine. Followers such as George Eliot and Harriet Martineau kept altruism and a humanity religion but rejected much of the system, and Brazilian republicans drew on its order-and-progress motto.
